 Commercial LPG Price Hiked by ₹10, ATF Rates Rise Again 
 National News Commercial LPG Price Hiked by ₹10, ATF Rates Rise Again
 Edited By : Ameya Sathaye Published : November 2, 2026, 5:47 AM IST   |   Updated : November 2, 2026, 5:47 AM IST   |   31 
 Share 0 
 Commercial LPG prices have increased by ₹10 per 19-kg cylinder to ₹2,820 from November 1, 2026. Aviation turbine fuel (ATF) rates have also risen by ₹1.37 per litre to ₹138.50. Domestic LPG, petrol and diesel prices remain unchanged, according to the latest revision by state-owned oil companies.
 Key Highlights 
 Commercial LPG prices rise by ₹10 to ₹2,820 per 19-kg cylinder.
 ATF prices increase by ₹1.37 to ₹138.50 per litre from November 1.
 Domestic LPG remains unchanged at ₹942 per 14.2-kg cylinder.
 Petrol and diesel prices remain unchanged despite the latest fuel price revision.
 New Delhi, Nov 02: Commercial LPG prices have been increased by ₹10 per 19-kg cylinder , taking the price to ₹2,820 from November 1, 2026. This is the second consecutive monthly increase after rates were raised by ₹62.50 on October 1. Prices had also increased by ₹9.50 on September 1, following two consecutive monthly reductions of ₹183.50 in July and ₹192 in August. The latest revision reflects changes in international energy benchmarks and the cost of fuel supplies.
 Commercial LPG prices have experienced significant fluctuations during the year. Between February and June, the price of a 19-kg cylinder increased by ₹1,373, rising from ₹1,740.50 to a record ₹3,113.50. Rates subsequently declined in July and August before the latest two monthly increases. According to the revised price list, a 5-kg Free Trade LPG (FTL) cylinder for a new connection costs ₹1,903 , while a refill is priced at ₹782. Meanwhile, domestic LPG prices have remained unchanged at ₹942 for a 14.2-kg cylinder, providing relief to household consumers. Petrol and diesel prices have also remained unchanged following the increases of around ₹7.50 per litre each in May.
 In another revision effective November 1, aviation turbine fuel (ATF) prices have increased by ₹1.37 per litre to ₹138.50 , compared with ₹137.12 previously. This marks the fourth consecutive monthly increase in jet fuel prices, driven by firm international benchmark rates. ATF is a major cost component for airlines, accounting for up to 40 per cent of their operating expenses. Continued increases in jet fuel prices can therefore add to the operating cost pressures faced by domestic and international airlines.
 The monthly revisions in LPG and ATF prices are based on movements in international benchmark rates and the rupee-dollar exchange rate. State-owned oil marketing companies revise these prices on the first day of every month. The actual retail rates may vary across states because of local taxes, including value-added tax (VAT). The latest changes highlight the contrasting impact on commercial fuel users and households, with commercial LPG and aviation fuel becoming more expensive while domestic cooking gas, petrol and diesel prices remain unchanged.
 The November 2026 fuel price revision brings another increase for commercial LPG consumers and the aviation sector. While commercial cylinder and ATF rates have moved higher, unchanged domestic LPG, petrol and diesel prices offer some stability to household and vehicle owners.
